Subject: Unexpected April allocation: session attribution looks off

Hi Jonas,

We're seeing a ~40% increase in billed tokens for April versus March without a matching uptick in calls. Attached is a small export (usage_export_202704.csv) showing a sample of sessions where token counts jump even though session lengths are identical.

We suspect there's double-counting when a migration token was in-flight — our eng team noticed two API keys used briefly during a rollout. Could that cause token attribution to be applied twice? The charges are material for our month-end reconciliation and we need an explanation and proposed remediation.

Can you take a look or point me to the right team?

Thanks,
Sarah Ng

Hi Sarah — thanks for the examples and for flagging this. Initial findings from a quick reconciliation: we found ~1.2M tokens in April tied to two distinct API keys that were both mapped to Edgecase's org during a short migration window (2027-04-07 03:00 - 03:20 UTC). Our pipeline attributes token usage to the API key present on the request; when keys are rotated mid-session we have a guard that should unify attribution via request_id, but in this case several request IDs arrived split across two backend events and the de-duplication check missed them because the request hash included a transient session suffix from your rollout tooling.

What this means practically: a small subset of long-running sessions (approx. 0.8% of sessions in that 20-minute window) had their prefix tokens counted twice when the second event was recorded. That lines up with your CSV sample where identical session durations show divergent token totals.

Remediation options we propose:
- Apply a targeted credit for the duplicated tokens for April (we calculated a conservative credit to cover 100% of the duplicated tokens we found).
- Patch our de-duplication layer to ignore the transient session suffix seen in your rollout (Marcus will lead this and schedule a deploy — low risk).
- Provide you with a sanitized export of all affected request IDs for your records.

I'll attach a short credit proposal PDF and the affected request ID list if you'd like.

Laura Bennett
Billing Ops Manager, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachment: proposed_credit_0407.pdf (PDF, 8KB)

Date: 2027-05-23T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected April allocation: session attribution looks off

Thanks Laura — adding the technical detail here for transparency. Root cause summary: during the key rollover, the second event that closed out some long-lived sessions included a session-id suffix produced by Edgecase's rollout script ("-ro-v1"). Our hash normalization step didn't strip that suffix, so de-dup failed. We'll roll a fix that strips a configurable suffix list and re-run the dedupe for the window.

Estimate for impact and credit: we scanned the affected window; duplicate tokens total 1,238,600 tokens. At Edgecase's plan rate that equates to $3,714.60. Proposal: issue a one-time invoice credit of $3,715 (rounded). Laura — please confirm the credit memo and how you'd like to present it (on next invoice vs retrospective refund).

Marcus Lin
